title: Hoop Pine: Ancient Hoop Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: The Queensland conifer with barrel hoops on its bark. A 33-metre one in Brisbane, one by Yarra Boulevard, and San Diego's, in a photograph of 1913.
intro: The name is on the trunk. A hoop pine's bark is ringed at intervals with raised bands, stacked like the hoops on a barrel. Araucaria cunninghamii is a rainforest conifer of Queensland and northern New South Wales, a relative of the monkey puzzle and the Norfolk Island pine, and its timber was the softwood Queensland's sawmills ran on for generations. In Brisbane's City Botanic Gardens, one stands on raised ground inside the George Street fence, 33 metres high; the National Trust's register put it at roughly sixty years in 2014. In Melbourne, another grows beside Yarra Boulevard, 3.46 metres round and already over a hundred years old by the City of Yarra's register in 2012. San Diego's has the best paper trail. Kensington was laid out in 1910, and a photograph of 1913 already shows this hoop pine in the park by today's library, in the spot where it stands now. Every December the neighbourhood lights it.
